class cccma_ppp.data_modules.dataset.dataset_abc.DatasetConfigABC

Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for configuring pipeline datasets.

Defines the shared interface for selecting model and conditioning data, resolving conditioning methods, validating compatibility between data sources, and selecting forecast lead times. Train and Inference datasets inherit from this class to implement specific data-loading.

Supports ensemble-mean, cross-ensemble, same-member, and static conditioning. Model data can also serve as the conditioning source when a separate conditioning dataset is not provided.

Subclasses must implement available_times, ds_operator, effective_input, and build_dataset. The following attributes must be defined in subclasses including both Train and Inference pipelines:

model

Configuration for the model prediction data. Could only be None for Inference pipeline where the conditioning dataset must provide the required input.

Type:

ModelDataConfig | None

condition

Optional configuration for auxiliary conditioning data. If None, model data may be reused as conditioning data, depending on the selected conditioning method.

Type:

ConditionDataConfig | None

condition_method

Method used to associate conditioning data with model inputs. Supported methods are “ensemble_mean”, “cross_ensemble”, “same_member”, and “static”.

Type:

str | None

lead_times

Requested forecast lead times. Accepts a lead-time configuration or an explicit sequence. If None, all available input lead times are selected.

Type:

lead_time_config | list | np.ndarray | None

abstract property available_times

Return the time span available for dataset construction. This is different than input time because it should be the common time range resolved by the forecast and if available, the observation data. Forecasts range is based on initialization time and lead time, while observation data has one time resolution.

For instance, for decadal predictions, the initial times are the start of the years, but the available times are the span of coverage based on initial_time / lead_time span which has a monthly resolution.

Subclasses must implement this property to determine which initialization times satisfy their input and target data requirements.

abstractmethod build_dataset()

Construct the dataset from this validated configuration.

Subclasses must implement this method to assemble the required model, conditioning, and optional observational data according to their dataset-specific sampling and preprocessing procedures.

condition: ConditionDataConfig | None
condition_method: str | None
abstract property ds_operator

Return the dataset-specific operator.

Subclasses must implement this property to provide the operator used for their dataset construction and data access.

Recommended implementaion is from cccma_ppp.data_modules.dataset.operator import DatasetOperator.

property effective_condition: ConditionDataConfig | ModelDataConfig | None

Return the resolved conditioning data. Resolved at __init__ time based on the provided model and condition configs.

Returns:

Explicit or model-derived conditioning configuration, or None if no conditioning dataset is required.

Return type:

ConditionDataConfig | ModelDataConfig | None

property effective_condition_method: str

Return the normalized conditioning method.

Returns:

Lowercase conditioning method, or None if no method is specified.

Return type:

str | None

abstract property effective_input: ConditionDataConfig | ModelDataConfig | None

Return the input data that effectively goes into the dataset. For Inference and Train this shall differ based on what is provided in the config.

Subclasses must implement this property to identify the data source used as the primary input.

Returns:

Effective input configuration.

Return type:

ConditionDataConfig | ModelDataConfig | None

final get_input_times(requested_times: Sequence[datetime64 | datetime | datetime] | ndarray | DataArray)

Resolve requested initialization times against the effective input.

Validates that all requested times are available to the dataset, and selects those present in the effective input’s initialization-time coordinates to iterate over.

The intention for this code is the dataset available temporal coverage is based on the model/condition/observation common time span. But, the exact initial times to be iterated over is not necessarily the same as the available times. See documentation for available_times for more details.

Parameters:

requested_times (Sequence[np.datetime64 | datetime.datetime | cftime.datetime] | np.ndarray | xr.DataArray) – Requested initialization times. Non-xarray inputs are converted to a DataArray indexed by the initialization-time dimension.

Returns:

Requested initialization times that are present in the effective input dataset, preserving their original order.

Return type:

xr.DataArray

Raises:

ValueError – If any requested initialization time is not included in available_times.

class cccma_ppp.data_modules.dataset.dataset_abc.lead_time_config(list_lead_times: list | None = None, start: int = 1, end: int = None)

Bases: object

Configuration for selecting forecast lead times.

Supports either an explicit list of lead times or an inclusive range defined by starting and ending lead times. Lead times are one-based.

Parameters:

  • list_lead_times (list | None, default None) – Explicit list of lead times to select. If provided, start and end are ignored.

  • start (int, default 1) – First lead time in the selected range. Used only when list_lead_times is None.

  • end (int | None, default None) – Last lead time in the selected range, inclusive. Required when list_lead_times is None.

build_lead_times()

Construct the selected forecast lead times.

Returns the explicitly specified lead times, if available. Otherwise, generates an inclusive sequence from start to end.

Returns:

Selected lead times. Returns the original list when list_lead_times is provided.

Return type:

list | np.ndarray

end: int = None
list_lead_times: list | None = None
start: int = 1
